data.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 27 at 1:25AM EDT until October 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph Metro
and coastal areas of Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward, Coastal Miami Dade, Coastal Palm Beach,
Metro Broward, Metro Palm Beach, and Metropolitan Miami Dade
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
data.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

data.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 27 at 1:22AM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT early
this morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
data.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 271122
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
722 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

...New UPDATE, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 714 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

 - Major coastal flooding is expected with each high tide cycle
   over the next couple of days. Inundated roadways will be likely
   for coastal areas.
 
 - Locally heavy rain may produce isolated minor urban flooding.

 - Strong winds, with gusts over 35 mph are possible through
   Tuesday night.

 - Dangerous marine and beach conditions are expected through the
   middle of the week.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 722 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Only update this morning was to lower PoPs a little across the 
area for today given latest trends and consensus of short-range 
models which indicate rain chances more in the 40-60% range over 
east coast metro areas. This represents little overall change in 
the weather scenario for today which will feature quick-moving 
showers with brief bursts of moderate to heavy rainfall, as well
as gusty NE winds. Also reduced thunder chances to 20% or less 
due to prevalence of dry air aloft and deepest moisture and 
highest instability over the Bahamas.

Tide levels at the east coast sites are on track to reach moderate
to borderline major flood levels in the next 2-3 hours.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Wednesday)
Issued at 201 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

The pattern for the middle of this week remains largely unchanged 
with a mid-level low remaining mostly stationary near the Bahamas 
today before finally advecting eastward for the end of the week as 
the ridge blocking pattern over the eastern US begins to break down. 
The surface high pressure in the northeast will remain amplified for 
one more day, resulting in another round of gusty NE winds today due 
to the potent pressure gradient. Expect wind gusts today again in 
the 30-40 mph range consistently along the east coast metro and 
beaches today with sustained winds often in the 25-30 mph range. 
Coastal showers will be likely once again throughout the day due to 
speed/frictional convergence occurring as stronger winds over the 
water merge into slightly weaker winds right over the adjacent land 
areas. Rainfall from these swiftly moving showers are not expected 
to be enough to result in a risk for excessive rainfall, despite a 
surface low likely advecting across the area from the east. This 
surface low could provide enough forcing for some slightly extra 
rainfall, but still not anticipated to be enough to result in 
excessive rainfall. High temperatures today are primarily expected 
in the low to mid 80s. 

As the low near the Bahamas begins its northward/north-eastward 
shift, the local pressure gradient will start to relax for the 
latter half of Wednesday as mid-level troughing advecting across the 
central US helps to weaken the stout high pressure in the northeast 
US, although breezy northeasterly winds are still expected to linger 
through Wednesday across South Florida. The low near the Bahamas 
will be the primary forcing mechanism for showers and storms, with 
our region sitting on the western periphery of the circulation. 
Enough vorticity and additional forcing should provide enough energy 
for scattered showers and some thunderstorms across the region. Most 
of this is projected to be of the weaker variety with low chances 
for a couple of heavier downpours. High temperatures are expected to 
rise to the mid to upper 80s for Wednesday.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Wednesday night through Monday)
Issued at 201 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

After fruitful talks with the wind, an agreement has been reached 
for an immediate ceasing of its northeasterly onslaught of the 
Florida Atlantic coast. This calming of the winds shall commence 
early Thursday morning as pressure gradients finally begin to relax 
across South Florida. While surface high pressure off the coast of 
the mid-Atlantic United States will still be quite strong, it's 
influence over the winds in South Florida will begin to diminish as 
the main centroid drifts further east into the ocean. Meanwhile, 
surface troughing along the northern Caribbean will also begin to 
wash out as a weakening surface low drifts west into the Gulf. This 
will allow for wind directions to finally change (after about a week 
of northeast flow) to a more easterly direction. Wind speeds will 
lessen to 5 to 8 mph, and a more typical sea-breeze pattern may 
actually be able to develop during the afternoon (although the 
westerly Gulf breeze will likely struggle to push far inland). 

Relating to the pattern aloft, ensemble guidance is in good 
agreement regarding the evolution of the cut-off mid level low over 
the Bahamas. This feature should finally eject east into the 
Atlantic by end of the day Thursday. This will allow for ridging 
from the Gulf to expand across the Florida peninsula through the 
weekend. Guidance is hinting that 500 mb heights may climb into the 
588 to 591 dam range, which would be above the 75th percentile for 
this time of year. This pattern should result in temperatures 
warming back up into the mid to upper 80s across South Florida and 
overall less unsettled weather. But, with PWATs hanging around at 
1.6 to 1.8 inches, PoPs will still be around 30% to 40% across most 
of the region. Continued east to northeast flow will keep the 
highest chances for showers and thunderstorms over interior and 
southwest Florida, closer to the Gulf breeze convergence. Overnight, 
isolated to scattered showers will continue to be a nuisance along 
Atlantic coastal areas. Luckily for you trick or treaters on 
Halloween night, the weather is looking quite nice, with only about 
a 20% chance of showers along eastern metro areas and light to calm 
winds from the east.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 722 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

VFR conditions to prevail with brief MVFR conditions possible in
quick-moving SHRA throughout most of the forecast period. This
scenario covered by PROB30 SHRA but some sites may see very little
in the way of ceiling/visibility reductions. TSRA chances too low
to mention. Winds 020-040 degrees 15-20 knots gusting to as high
as 25-30 knots, gradually becoming 050-070 degrees 12-15 knots
with gusts around 20 knots after 04z-06z.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 201 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Hazardous marine conditions will continue through at least mid-week 
as strong northeasterly winds persist across the local waters. 
Frequent gusts to gale force are expected through Tuesday night 
across the Atlantic waters, where a Gale Warning remains in effect. 
Small Craft Advisory conditions will continue across the Gulf waters 
and Lake Okeechobee through at least Wednesday, with the Gale 
Warning becoming a Small Craft Advisory in the Atlantic on Tuesday 
night. Seas are forecast at 5 to 8 feet in the Gulf today and 10 to 
14 feet across the Atlantic waters. Scattered to numerous showers 
and isolated storms are also expected to develop across the Atlantic 
waters over the next several days. These hazardous conditions should 
gradually improve toward the end of the week.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 201 AM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

A high risk of rip currents will persist for all Atlantic beaches 
through at least mid-week period. Dangerous surf heights of 8 to 11 
feet are expected to linger for the Palm Beaches through Wednesday.

Furthermore, strong onshore wind flow and high seas may combine with 
King Tides to increase the threat of coastal flooding along the 
Atlantic coast. Today and tomorrow have the highest chances for 
reaching major flood stage, with moderate flooding otherwise 
occurring at minimum. Therefore, a Coastal Flood Warning is in 
effect along the Atlantic coast through Wednesday due to the 
potential for significant coastal flooding. 

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Miami            82  75  85  75 /  60  60  30  20 
West Kendall     84  75  86  75 /  50  50  30  10 
Opa-Locka        83  75  86  74 /  60  60  30  20 
Homestead        84  75  86  75 /  50  50  20  20 
Fort Lauderdale  81  75  84  75 /  60  60  40  30 
N Ft Lauderdale  82  75  84  75 /  60  60  40  40 
Pembroke Pines   84  74  86  74 /  60  60  40  20 
West Palm Beach  82  74  84  74 /  70  70  50  30 
Boca Raton       82  75  84  75 /  60  60  50  40 
Naples           85  72  87  73 /  10  10  40  10 

&&

.MFL WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...Wind Advisory until 8 PM EDT this evening for FLZ068-072-074-168-
     172-173.

     Coastal Flood Warning until 8 PM EDT Wednesday for FLZ168-172-
     173.

     High Rip Current Risk through Wednesday evening for FLZ168-172-
     173.

     High Surf Advisory until 8 PM EDT Wednesday for FLZ168.

AM...Small Craft Advisory until 8 PM EDT Wednesday for AMZ610.

     Gale Warning until 8 AM EDT Wednesday for AMZ630-650-651-670-671.

     Small Craft Advisory from 8 AM to 8 PM EDT Wednesday for AMZ630-
     650-651-670-671.

GM...Small Craft Advisory until 8 PM EDT Wednesday for GMZ656-657-676.

&&
